comment: Built-in Windows firewall rule groups and rule IDs. Matching is locale-independent: 'groups' are raw group resource strings (case-insensitive), 'namePatterns' are rule ID wildcards. roles: needed | optional | bloat per role (Gamer, PowerUser, Sysadmin, Workstation); 'bloat' makes an enabled rule Bloated for that role. bloatWhen narrows bloat to a condition (packagesMissing: none of these packages installed). basis: microsoft (documented) or igwt (iG Windows Tuner judgement from the feature's purpose).

groups.name: Windows Service Hardening
groups.hint: Built-in restrictions that keep each Windows service to the network traffic it needs.
groups.meaning: Windows Service Hardening rules limit what each system service may send and receive, so a compromised service cannot use the network freely. They live in their own policy stores (the static store is read-only) and are not shown by the normal firewall console.
neededFor: Limiting what each Windows service can do on the network

groups.name: Core Networking
groups.hint: DHCP, DNS, IPv6 neighbor discovery, ICMPv6, IGMP and Teredo: what every PC needs to get an address and reach the network.
groups.meaning: The rules Windows uses for basic IP networking: getting an address (DHCP, DHCPv6), IPv6 router and neighbor discovery and the ICMPv6 messages IPv6 cannot work without, multicast membership (IGMP), DNS and the IPv6 transition technologies (Teredo, IP-HTTPS). Microsoft's deployment guidance keeps every Core Networking rule enabled.
groups.riskNote: Low surface: the rules are limited to the system services and message types they need.

groups.name: Core Networking Diagnostics
groups.hint: Answers ping (ICMP echo) requests. Off by default; useful for troubleshooting, not needed for normal use.
groups.meaning: Lets other devices ping this PC (ICMPv4 and ICMPv6 echo requests). Windows ships these rules disabled; administrators turn them on to test reachability.
groups.riskNote: Answering ping on Public networks makes the PC easier to find.

groups.name: Network Discovery
groups.hint: Lets this PC see and be seen by other devices on the local network (UPnP, SSDP, WSD, LLMNR, NetBIOS).
groups.meaning: Device discovery on the local network: UPnP and SSDP, Web Services for Devices, LLMNR and NetBIOS name lookups. Windows turns these on for Private networks when you choose to make the PC discoverable.
neededFor: Seeing other PCs, media devices and network printers in File Explorer
groups.riskNote: LLMNR and NetBIOS answers on untrusted networks can leak credentials (poisoning attacks); keep these rules off on Public networks.

groups.name: File and Printer Sharing
groups.hint: Shares folders and printers with other PCs (SMB 445, NetBIOS 137-139, print spooler, ping).
groups.meaning: Lets other PCs open shared folders and printers on this PC over SMB and the print spooler. The Restrictive variant limits the same features to the local subnet.
neededFor: Sharing folders or printers from this PC
Other PCs pinging this PC (FPS-ICMP rules)
groups.riskNote: SMB and NetBIOS reachable from untrusted networks are a common ransomware entry point; never allow them on Public.

groups.name: Remote Desktop
groups.hint: Lets others connect to this PC with Remote Desktop (TCP/UDP 3389, shadowing, WebSocket).
groups.meaning: Inbound Remote Desktop connections. Windows enables these rules when Remote Desktop is turned on in Settings.
neededFor: Connecting to this PC with Remote Desktop
groups.riskNote: RDP reachable from untrusted networks is a top ransomware entry point; allow it on Private or the local subnet only.

groups.name: Windows Remote Management
groups.hint: PowerShell remoting and WinRM (TCP 5985/5986, compatibility port 80).
groups.meaning: Inbound WS-Management for PowerShell remoting and remote administration tools. Turned on by Enable-PSRemoting or winrm quickconfig.
groups.riskNote: Remote administration from untrusted networks; keep it to Domain or Private.

groups.name: Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI)
groups.hint: Remote WMI queries and management (DCOM/RPC). Not needed for local WMI.
groups.meaning: Lets remote computers query and manage this PC through WMI over DCOM. Local WMI, which apps and Windows use all the time, does not need these rules.
neededFor: Remote WMI management and inventory tools

groups.name: Remote administration (event log, services, firewall, tasks, volumes, shutdown, event monitor)
groups.hint: Lets administrators manage this PC's event logs, services, firewall, tasks, disks and shutdown remotely (RPC).
groups.meaning: Remote management groups used by MMC consoles and server tools: Remote Event Log Management, Remote Service Management, Windows Defender Firewall Remote Management, Remote Scheduled Tasks Management, Remote Volume Management, Remote Shut-down, Remote Event Monitor and Performance Logs and Alerts.
neededFor: Managing this PC from another PC with MMC consoles or server tools
groups.riskNote: Each group opens RPC endpoints for remote administration.

groups.name: Remote Assistance
groups.hint: Lets a helper you invite view or control this PC (Easy Connect, PNRP, SSDP, DCOM).
groups.meaning: Windows Remote Assistance invitations and Easy Connect. Quick Assist, the modern replacement, does not use these rules.
neededFor: Receiving help through Windows Remote Assistance invitations
groups.riskNote: Opens discovery and DCOM endpoints for remote control.

groups.name: Windows Media Player sharing and Media Center Extenders
groups.hint: Legacy media streaming: Windows Media Player Network Sharing, Media Center Extenders (Xbox 360 era) and WMP network.
groups.meaning: DLNA media library sharing from the legacy Windows Media Player and Media Center Extender streaming to old set-top boxes and consoles.
neededFor: Streaming a legacy Windows Media Player library to DLNA devices
groups.riskNote: UPnP, SSDP and HTTP streaming listeners on the local network.

groups.name: Cast to Device, DIAL and Wireless Display
groups.hint: Casting video and screens to TVs and wireless displays (Miracast, DLNA Play To, DIAL).
groups.meaning: Cast to Device (Play To), the DIAL protocol server used by casting apps and Wireless Display (projecting to this PC or to a Miracast display).
neededFor: Projecting to or from a wireless display

groups.name: Wi-Fi Direct, proximity sharing and portable devices
groups.hint: Wi-Fi Direct printers and scanners, Nearby/proximity sharing and media devices over the network (MTP).
groups.meaning: Wi-Fi Direct discovery of printers and scanners, the Wi-Fi Direct services platform, proximity sharing and Wireless Portable Devices (MTP over the network).

groups.name: Peer to Peer Collaboration and PNRP
groups.hint: Legacy peer-to-peer collaboration (People Near Me, PNRP name registration). Unused by modern Windows apps.
groups.meaning: The Windows Peer-to-Peer Collaboration Foundation and the Peer Name Resolution Protocol computer-name registration, used by legacy collaboration apps.

groups.name: Server and enterprise features (iSCSI, DTC, RRAS, SSTP, KMS, SNMP, Netlogon, BranchCache)
groups.hint: Enterprise and server roles: iSCSI, Distributed Transactions, Routing/VPN server, KMS host, SNMP traps, Netlogon, BranchCache.
groups.meaning: Rules for features a home or gaming PC does not run: the iSCSI initiator service, the Distributed Transaction Coordinator, Routing and Remote Access (VPN server), the SSTP VPN server, a KMS activation host, SNMP traps, Netlogon and BranchCache content sharing.
neededFor: Corporate storage, VPN server, activation, monitoring and branch-office caching
groups.riskNote: Server listeners that should only exist where the role is used.

groups.name: AllJoyn Router and Connected Devices Platform
groups.hint: Device-to-device features: Phone Link, Nearby sharing, cross-device experiences (CDP) and legacy AllJoyn IoT.
groups.meaning: The Connected Devices Platform behind Phone Link, Nearby sharing and 'continue on PC', and the AllJoyn router for legacy smart-home devices.

groups.name: mDNS
groups.hint: Multicast DNS (UDP 5353): finds printers, casting targets and other devices by name on the local network.
groups.meaning: Multicast DNS name discovery, the modern replacement Microsoft is moving to from NetBIOS and LLMNR.
neededFor: Finding printers, TVs and other devices by name
groups.riskNote: Answers name queries on the local network; keep it off on Public networks.

groups.name: Delivery Optimization
groups.hint: Peer-to-peer download of Windows and Store updates (port 7680). Updates still download without it.
groups.meaning: Lets Delivery Optimization share update pieces with other PCs on the local network or the internet. Windows Update keeps working over HTTP without these rules.
neededFor: Sharing and receiving update pieces with other PCs

groups.name: Virtual Machine Monitoring
groups.hint: Lets a Hyper-V host monitor this PC when it runs as a virtual machine (RPC, DCOM, ping).
groups.meaning: Hyper-V integration rules used when this Windows runs as a guest virtual machine.
neededFor: Hyper-V host monitoring of this machine as a guest

groups.name: TPM Virtual Smart Card Management
groups.hint: Remote management of TPM virtual smart cards (DCOM). Used in corporate smart-card deployments.
groups.meaning: Lets administrators create and manage TPM virtual smart cards on this PC remotely.

groups.name: Windows Device Management (MDM enrollment)
groups.hint: Outbound rules for MDM enrollment and management (Intune and other MDM services).
groups.meaning: Outbound connections of the Windows MDM client: enrollment, certificate installation and OMA-DM management sessions.
neededFor: Enrolling and managing the PC with Intune or another MDM service

groups.name: Windows system outbound (troubleshooting, cloud identity, media source)
groups.hint: Windows components that connect out: recommended troubleshooting, cloud identity (Microsoft and work accounts), camera frame server.
groups.meaning: Outbound rules for Recommended Troubleshooting downloads, the Cloud Identity service used for Microsoft and work accounts, and the Media Foundation network source (network cameras).
neededFor: Signing in with Microsoft or work accounts

groups.name: Connected User Experiences and Telemetry
groups.hint: Outbound rule for Windows diagnostic data (DiagTrack). Diagnostic data is set in Settings or by the privacy tweaks.
groups.meaning: Lets the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service send diagnostic data. The amount of data is a policy setting; iG Windows Tuner handles it with the privacy items, not with firewall blocks.
groups.riskNote: Outbound only; blocking it with the firewall is not how Microsoft supports turning diagnostic data down.

groups.name: Windows Security and SmartScreen apps
groups.hint: Network access for the Windows Security app and Microsoft Defender SmartScreen.
groups.meaning: AppContainer rules for the Windows Security app and SmartScreen, which checks downloads and sites against Microsoft's reputation service.

groups.name: Xbox apps and Game Bar
groups.hint: Xbox app, Game Bar and Xbox sign-in. Needed for Game Pass and Xbox multiplayer and party chat.
groups.meaning: AppContainer rules of the Xbox apps: the Xbox app (Game Pass), Game Bar, the Xbox sign-in provider and the in-game UI. Xbox party chat and peer multiplayer also use Teredo from Core Networking, which stays on.
neededFor: Game Pass and the Xbox app

groups.name: Microsoft Store, App Installer and account apps
groups.hint: Store purchases and updates, winget (App Installer), Microsoft and work account sign-in, Wi-Fi sign-in pages.
groups.meaning: AppContainer rules for the Microsoft Store and its purchase host, App Installer (winget), the account sign-in brokers and the captive portal page used to sign in to public Wi-Fi.
neededFor: Signing in to Microsoft and work accounts

groups.name: Microsoft apps (Store packages)
groups.hint: Network access of Microsoft's own Store apps and Windows shell packages (Start, Calculator, Camera, Weather ...).
groups.meaning: Windows creates AppContainer rules for each Microsoft-published package that declares a network capability. The rule follows the app: removing the app removes its rules.
neededFor: The app the rule belongs to
groups.riskNote: AppContainer apps are sandboxed; the rule only gives the capability the app declared.
